guide.summary: The Temple of Speed: long straights, tiny wings, and Ferrari fans flooding the track after the race.
guide.character: The fastest lap of the season. Cars run their lowest downforce and are at full throttle for most of the lap. Races are won and lost under braking for the chicanes.

corners.name: Parabolica (Curva Alboreto)
corners.note: A long, fast right onto the main straight, renamed after Michele Alboreto in 2021.

corners.name: Ascari chicane
corners.note: A fast left-right-left. A good exit sets up the long run to the Parabolica.

moments.title: The closest finish ever
moments.body: Peter Gethin won the 1971 Italian GP by 0.01 seconds, and the first five cars crossed the line within 0.61 seconds of each other.

history.body: Built in the park of the royal villa at Monza.
In the first World Championship season and on the calendar every year since, except 1980.
Some races also used the banked oval.
Today's 5.793 km layout, after the first chicane was reshaped.

notes.championship: Race counts, wins and poles cover World Championship Grands Prix only, not non-championship races. The Indianapolis 500 (1950-1960) is left out of wins and poles.
notes.lapRecord: Race lap records count races from 2004 on: the race data has no fastest-lap times before 2004.
notes.poleRecord: Pole records use the pole-winning qualifying lap. Qualifying times are complete from 2003; 1994-2002 has some rounds only.
notes.raceLaps: Race laps is the scheduled distance: the lap count most winners on the layout completed, so shortened races don't change it.
